title: The Deccan Sultanates
subtitle: The Bahmanis and the five Shahi kingdoms · 1347 – 1687
subject: deccan-sultanates
intro: In 1347 rebel nobles of the Delhi Sultanate founded the Bahmani Sultanate in the Deccan. After its great minister Mahmud Gawan was executed it broke into five kingdoms: the Adil Shahis of Bijapur, the Nizam Shahis of Ahmadnagar, the Qutb Shahis of Golconda, the Imad Shahis of Berar and the Barid Shahis of Bidar. They fought Vijayanagara and one another, united to win at Talikota in 1565, and built Bijapur, Hyderabad and the Charminar. Shahaji Bhonsle served them, and his son Shivaji founded the Maratha state at their expense. The Mughals absorbed them one by one, ending with Golconda in 1687.

events.title: Bahman Shah founds the Bahmani Sultanate
events.summary: Rebel nobles of the Delhi Sultanate in the Deccan elect Hasan Gangu as their sultan. Taking the title Alauddin Bahman Shah, he rules from Gulbarga.

events.title: Mohammed Shah I organises the state
events.summary: Bahman Shah's son divides the kingdom into four provinces under governors (tarafdars) and fights the first wars with Vijayanagara.

events.title: First war over the Raichur Doab
events.summary: Mohammed Shah I and Bukka Raya I of Vijayanagara fight a savage war over the land between the Krishna and the Tungabhadra — the start of two centuries of conflict.

events.title: Great mosque at Gulbarga
events.summary: The Jama Masjid inside Gulbarga fort is completed — a hall roofed entirely with domes and no open courtyard.

events.title: Firuz Shah Bahmani
events.summary: Firuz Shah, scholar and builder, takes the throne. He recruits Persian and Arab migrants to his court and campaigns against Vijayanagara.

events.title: Bande Nawaz settles at Gulbarga
events.summary: The Chishti saint Bande Nawaz (Gesu Daraz) arrives from Delhi; his dargah at Gulbarga becomes the Deccan's great Sufi shrine.

events.title: Defeat at Pangal
events.summary: Firuz Shah's army is routed by Vijayanagara at the siege of Pangal; he is forced to abdicate for his brother Ahmad.

events.title: Ahmad Shah Wali takes the throne
events.summary: Firuz's brother Ahmad Shah becomes sultan and later conquers Warangal from the Kakatiyas' successors.

events.title: The capital moves to Bidar
events.summary: Ahmad Shah Wali moves the capital from Gulbarga to Bidar and rebuilds its fort.

events.title: Deccanis against newcomers
events.summary: Court politics split between the 'Deccanis', long-settled Muslims, and the 'Afaqis', newly arrived Persians and Turks — a feud that later breaks the kingdom.

events.title: Mahmud Gawan becomes chief minister
events.summary: Under the boy king Muhammad Shah III, the Persian merchant-statesman Mahmud Gawan reforms the provinces and the army.

events.title: A Russian at Bidar
events.summary: The Tver merchant Afanasy Nikitin spends years in the Bahmani kingdom and describes Bidar's splendour and the poverty of the countryside.

events.title: Goa taken from Vijayanagara
events.summary: Mahmud Gawan's campaigns capture Goa and the west-coast ports, giving the Bahmanis the horse trade with Arabia and Persia.

events.title: Mahmud Gawan's madrasa
events.summary: Gawan builds a three-storey college at Bidar faced with glazed tiles, with a library said to hold thousands of books.

events.title: Mahmud Gawan executed
events.summary: Rivals forge a letter of treason; the drunken sultan has Gawan beheaded. The kingdom never recovers its unity.

events.title: The governors declare independence
events.summary: Yusuf Adil Khan at Bijapur, Ahmad Nizam-ul-Mulk at Ahmadnagar and Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk in Berar stop obeying Bidar; Qasim Barid controls the sultan himself.

events.title: Ahmadnagar founded
events.summary: Ahmad Nizam Shah builds a new capital, Ahmadnagar, on the Sina river.

events.title: Portuguese take Goa from Bijapur
events.summary: Afonso de Albuquerque storms Goa; the Adil Shahis lose their main port.

events.title: Quli Qutb Mulk at Golconda
events.summary: The Turkman governor of Telangana, Quli Qutb Mulk, rules independently from Golconda fort.

events.title: Battle of Raichur
events.summary: Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara defeats Ismail Adil Shah and takes Raichur.

events.title: The last Bahmani sultan flees
events.summary: Kalimullah, last of the Bahmani line, escapes his Barid minders; the Bahmani Sultanate is over.

events.title: Battle of Talikota
events.summary: Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar unite against Vijayanagara and kill Rama Raya; the victors sack Hampi.

events.title: Ahmadnagar annexes Berar
events.summary: Murtaza Nizam Shah conquers the Imad Shahi kingdom of Berar.

events.title: Chand Bibi regent at Bijapur
events.summary: After Ali Adil Shah I is murdered, his widow Chand Bibi, a Nizam Shahi princess, guards the boy king Ibrahim II.

events.title: Hyderabad and the Charminar
events.summary: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, poet in Dakhini and Telugu, founds Hyderabad beside Golconda with the Charminar at its centre.

events.title: Chand Bibi defends Ahmadnagar
events.summary: Back in Ahmadnagar, Chand Bibi holds the fort against Prince Murad's Mughal army and forces a truce.

events.title: Ahmadnagar falls to the Mughals
events.summary: Chand Bibi is killed and the city taken, but Nizam Shahi loyalists fight on from the west.

events.title: Ibrahim II's Kitab-i-Nauras
events.summary: Ibrahim Adil Shah II writes songs in Dakhini invoking Saraswati and the Prophet alike; Bijapur becomes a centre of music and Deccan painting.

events.title: Malik Ambar founds Khadki
events.summary: Malik Ambar, an Ethiopian-born general who runs the Nizam Shahi state, builds a new capital at Khadki, later Aurangabad.

events.title: Malik Ambar's revenue settlement
events.summary: Malik Ambar surveys the land and fixes the revenue in cash; his system is later taken up by the Mughals in the Deccan.

events.title: Bijapur annexes Bidar
events.summary: Ibrahim Adil Shah II absorbs the last Barid Shahi territory.

events.title: Battle of Bhatvadi
events.summary: Malik Ambar's light cavalry — with the young Shahaji Bhonsle among his officers — defeats a combined Mughal–Bijapur army.

events.title: Malik Ambar dies
events.summary: Malik Ambar dies at about eighty; without him the Nizam Shahi state soon collapses.

events.title: Ibrahim Rauza
events.summary: Ibrahim II's tomb and mosque at Bijapur are finished — the elegant model, it is said, for the Taj Mahal's builders.

events.title: Shahaji's puppet sultan
events.summary: After the Mughals capture Daulatabad, Shahaji Bhonsle crowns a boy of the Nizam Shahi line and fights on in his name.

events.title: The Deccan settlement of 1636
events.summary: Shah Jahan ends the Nizam Shahi kingdom; Bijapur and Golconda accept Mughal overlordship and pay tribute.

events.title: Gol Gumbaz
events.summary: Mohammed Adil Shah's tomb is completed — one of the largest domes in the world, with a whispering gallery.

events.title: Aurangzeb attacks Golconda
events.summary: Prince Aurangzeb, viceroy of the Deccan, besieges Golconda; Shah Jahan orders him to make peace for a large indemnity.

events.title: Bijapur's general killed by Shivaji
events.summary: Bijapur sends Afzal Khan to destroy Shivaji; he is killed at Pratapgad and his army routed.

events.title: Jai Singh fails before Bijapur
events.summary: Jai Singh, with Shivaji's troops alongside, marches on Bijapur but has to retreat.

events.title: Madanna and Akkanna
events.summary: Abul Hasan Qutb Shah hands the government to the Brahmin brothers Madanna and Akkanna.

events.title: Golconda allies with Shivaji
events.summary: Shivaji is received in Hyderabad; with Golconda's money he campaigns in the Carnatic.

events.title: Bijapur falls
events.summary: After a fifteen-month siege Sikandar Adil Shah surrenders to Aurangzeb.

events.title: Golconda falls
events.summary: A gate is opened by treachery after an eight-month siege; Abul Hasan is taken prisoner and the last Deccan sultanate ends.
